soundness_flags.one_line: The model class encodes only a common order, not Bystrova--Devijver's intervention restriction that each environment retains a subset of baseline parents; hence its Theorem 1 cannot yet be invoked for every declared SCM pair.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 2--3, Assumption 1 and Definition 1; p. 7, Assumption 3; p. 10, Theorem 1
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper restricts interventions to existing baseline-parent relations, derives a shared topological order, defines diff-faithfulness as regression equality iff diff-separation, and proves LDiffPC recovers the skeleton with only correct orientations under perfect equality information.

source_verification_receipts.locator: publication page, abstract and bibliographic record, pp. 15--30
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The proceedings paper exists as claimed and studies identification of direct effects in linear difference-graph models; the accessible arXiv v2 corroborates the common-single-door direct-effect setting, while exact PMLR theorem-number verification remains a source-check item.
The paper gives a necessary-and-sufficient identification criterion for MPDAGs, which is graph-only and therefore orthogonal to paired covariance-ledger constraints.
The half-trek criterion gives polynomial-time sufficient generic-identifiability checks and a distinct obstruction for linear SEMs, not a paired-difference-graph ledger algorithm.
The paper gives constructive adjustment-set and separator algorithms for DAGs/MAGs, not algebraic compatibility over multiple covariance completions.

The paper concerns direct difference-DAG recovery from two linear SEMs under topological-layer conditions and allows differing noise variances; it does not subsume the proposed direct-effect completion problem.
